result.summary: This agreement sets out the terms for Alex Morgan to design and build a website for Northwind Digital Ltd. It lasts for twelve months with automatic renewal and heavily favors the Client through unlimited liability, strict non-compete clauses, and broad intellectual property assignment. Payment terms are lengthy at 90 days, and the Client can withhold funds if unsatisfied or change the scope without adjusting fees.

quote.text: This Agreement is made on 1 October 2026 between Northwind Digital Ltd ("the Client") and Alex Morgan ("the Contractor

quote.text: Fees" means the amounts set out in Schedule A

risks.title: Uncapped Liability and Indemnity
risks.plain_language: The Contractor is liable for all losses suffered by the Client without limit and must indemnify the Client against third-party claims relating to the Deliverables.
risks.why_it_matters: An unlimited liability exposes you to catastrophic financial risk if the client claims heavy losses, and indemnities can force you to pay for legal claims brought by outsiders.

quotes.text: The Contractor is liable for all losses suffered by the Client arising from the Services, without limit
The Contractor will indemnify the Client against any claim by a third party relating to the Deliverables

risks.title: Global Non-Competition Clause
risks.plain_language: For twenty-four months after the agreement ends, the Contractor cannot provide services to any business that competes with the Client anywhere in the world.
risks.why_it_matters: A worldwide ban on working with competing businesses for two years can severely restrict your ability to earn a living in your field.

quotes.text: For twenty-four (24) months after this Agreement ends, the Contractor will not provide services to any business that competes with the Client anywhere in the world

risks.title: Loss of Intellectual Property and Portfolio Rights
risks.plain_language: All rights in the Deliverables, including pre-existing materials you owned before the agreement, are assigned to the Client on creation. You also cannot show the work in your portfolio without written consent.
risks.why_it_matters: You immediately lose ownership of your pre-existing tools and draft materials, and you cannot use the finished project to market your freelance services to future clients.

quotes.text: All rights in the Deliverables, including any pre-existing materials of the Contractor used in them, are assigned to the Client on creation
The Contractor may not show the Deliverables in a portfolio without the Client's prior written consent

risks.title: One-Sided Scope and Payment Terms
risks.plain_language: The Client can change the project scope without increasing fees unless they agree otherwise in writing. Payment takes ninety days, can be withheld if the client is unsatisfied, and late invoices are permanently unpaid.
risks.why_it_matters: You may be forced to do extra work for free, wait three months to get paid, forfeit payment entirely if an invoice is late by even a day, or go unpaid if the client simply claims un-satisfaction.

quotes.text: The Client may change the scope of the Services at any time by written notice. The Fees will not change unless the Client agrees otherwise in writing
The Client will pay the Fees within ninety (90) days of receiving a valid invoice
The Client may withhold any payment if it is not satisfied with the Deliverables
Invoices must be submitted within 14 days of completing a milestone; late invoices will not be paid

risks.title: One-Sided Termination Rights and Forfeiture
risks.plain_language: The Client can terminate immediately at any time, while the Contractor must give 90 days' notice. Upon termination, the Client only pays for Deliverables it has accepted.
risks.why_it_matters: If the client terminates abruptly, you may lose months of unaccepted work without compensation, while being locked in for a long notice period if you want to leave.

quotes.text: The Client may terminate this Agreement at any time with immediate effect. The Contractor may terminate on ninety (90) days' written notice
On termination the Client will pay only for Deliverables it has accepted

risks.title: Unilateral Changes and Dispute Waiver
risks.plain_language: The Client can update terms by posting them on a portal, with continued work counting as acceptance. Disputes go to binding arbitration in London, and you waive the right to class actions.
risks.why_it_matters: Rules can change without your direct consent, and you give up your right to go to court or join forces with other contractors in a class action.

quotes.text: The Client may update these terms by posting a new version on its supplier portal. Continued work by the Contractor means acceptance
Any dispute will be resolved by binding arbitration in London. The Contractor waives any right to bring or join a class or collective action

Section 3.2 & 8.3: How can we protect against the client withholding payment arbitrarily or refusing to pay for unaccepted work upon termination?

Discuss the contract with a qualified lawyer before signing next week.
